historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (FY2022-FY2025, the first clean post-Refinitiv window), corroborated by the 7.0-7.5% FY2026 organic guidance and the 'mid to high single digit' 2027-29 framework
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGRs are unusable: +39.7%/yr over 5 years is the FY2021 Refinitiv share issue (equity 3.7bn -> 23.6bn) and -9.1%/yr over 3 years is £6bn of buybacks plus PPA amortisation. Statutory EPS is distorted by £1.0-1.5bn/yr of purchased-intangible amortisation (3yr CAGR 0.6% vs adjusted EPS +15.7% in FY2025 alone) and the FY2021 £2.6bn disposal gain. The 5yr revenue and FCF CAGRs (30.8%, 28.4%) span the acquisition and are not organic.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest income not stripped, net debt company): FY2020 706, FY2021 1,799, FY2022 1,613, FY2023 1,715, FY2024 2,226, FY2025 2,461. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR 15.1% vs reported 14.2%: SBC (158 -> 176) has grown slower than cash flow, so none of the reported growth is being paid for in stock. FCF growth has outrun income growth (6.5%) because of margin expansion (EBITDA 45.8% -> 50.3%) and capex intensity falling from 12.5% to 10.5% of income.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance delivered and the medium-term framework met at its midpoint. Subscription businesses (D&A, FTSE Russell, Risk Intelligence; ASV +6.1%) accelerate modestly as Workspace migration completes and AI-ready data (LSEG Everywhere, MCP, Microsoft/Google/Amazon integrations) is monetised through usage-based pricing; Markets (Tradeweb, LCH) grows above group but normalises from 2025-26's elevated volumes; net treasury income is roughly flat as rates settle. EBITDA margin reaches 53-54% on operating leverage and the end of Refinitiv integration costs; capex intensity falls to ~8.4%. Cash tax rises toward the 24-25% underlying rate as the US intangible tax amortisation runs off, and Tradeweb's minority takes a slowly rising ~10-10.5% of EBIT. Growth fades to 3% by year 10; Gordon at 8%/2.5% (18.6x) binds below the 20x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI monetisation is real and visible: usage-based data access and agentic workflows lift D&A to high-single-digit growth, FTSE Russell and Risk Intelligence sustain ~10%, Tradeweb keeps compounding ADV and expands into prediction markets and new asset classes, and LCH SwapClear's larger revenue share plus RepoClear volumes carry Post Trade. Income grows 8% for three years, fading to 4.5%; margin reaches 56% as the product-led operating model takes out cost faster than guided. Elliott Management's activism adds a capital-discipline and portfolio-simplification catalyst toward the multiples of S&P Global, MSCI and ICE, though no re-rating is modelled. Terminal growth 3%; the 20x cap binds (Gordon would be 20.6x). Weight is held at 25% because this needs three independent things to go right: AI pricing power, continued Tradeweb outgrowth and above-guidance cost-out.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI disintermediation of the terminal and desktop data model: Workspace seats and content licensing come under price pressure as customers route LLM agents to raw data, retention slips below 92% and D&A growth falls to low single digits. Lower rates compress net treasury income on clearing collateral; Tradeweb and LCH volumes normalise after a strong 2025-26; a stronger pound shrinks reported USD income. Income grows 5% then 2.5-3%, margin stalls around 50.5% as investment in AI and platform capacity continues without the revenue, capex intensity stays at 9%. Cash tax and NCI leakage ramp as in base. No solvency axis: leverage sits mid-range at 2.1x on A-rated debt, so the bear case is a multiple de-rating on slower growth, not distress.

valuation_philosophy.summary: LSEG is valued as an operating company on fully SBC-expensed, unlevered owner free cash flow, with the clearing house treated as an operating business (collateral balances ignored, net treasury income kept as revenue) and the Tradeweb/LCH/PTS minorities charged as a leakage on EBIT rather than deducted at book or market. The headline is the 25/50/25 probability-weighted value; the terminal value is bounded by the lower of Gordon at 8%/2.5% and 20x year-10 FCF. The entry price demands a 15% IRR with the terminal value rebuilt at that rate. House and street bases differ only by the ~1.9%-of-income SBC charge, so the band is narrow.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI disintermediation of desktop/terminal data (Workspace) and content licensing: the bear axis on the ~70% subscription base; retention 92.8% and ASV +6.1% are the KPIs to watch.
Net treasury income (£257m FY2025, ~6% of EBITDA) is a function of policy rates and clearing-member cash balances; a 200bp rate cut takes a meaningful slice of margin.
NCI treatment: Tradeweb's minority is charged at ~10% of EBIT in the flows; valuing it at market (~£9-11bn) instead would lower the weighted value by roughly £8-10/share (800-1,000p).

Cash tax runs ~12% of EBIT against a 24-25% underlying rate; the model ramps it to 24.5% by 2033 as US tax amortisation of acquired intangibles expires. If the shelter ends sooner, or the OECD Pillar Two top-up bites, value falls; if it persists longer the model is conservative.
Translation: ~45% of income is USD; the FY2026 guide is struck at GBPUSD 1.32. Each 5% move in GBPUSD is ~2% of income.
Markets volumes (Tradeweb ADV, LCH SwapClear/RepoClear) were elevated in 2025-26 on rate volatility; the base case assumes normalisation, not a step down.
Capex basis: the CSV capex (£985m) runs ~7% above the company's 'cash capex' (£919m); the projection is scaled to the CSV basis, which is the conservative side.
Terminal value is ~60% of EV at 8% WACC; each 50bp of WACC is worth roughly 8-9% of value (see sensitivity grid).

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 6,684-10,140p
data_sources.financials: LSEG.L_Metrics.csv / core_metrics and kpis (FY2018-FY2025 annual, H1 FY2025, H1 FY2026, Q1 FY2025, Q1 FY2026) derived from the annual reports and the H1 2026 interim (LSEG.L_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt: results table p.1, capital allocation p.8, outlook p.9, cash flow p.21, net debt p.22, notes 7 and 7.2); FY2025 Annual Report PPE note for ROU depreciation and the non-underlying D&A footnote
data_sources.qualitative: LSEG.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10: business model, moat, growth drivers, bull/bear cases, Elliott activism) plus the FY2025 Annual Report strategic report and the H1 2026 interim narrative (LSEG Everywhere, Workspace, Tradeweb, Post Trade Solutions)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 Total income incl. recoveries (£360m) and net treasury income (£257m), the base the adjusted EBITDA margin is struck on. Recoveries are pass-through third-party content fees; NTI is interest earned on clearing-member collateral and is an operating income line of LCH, not finance income.
inputs.share_count_basis: 488m ordinary shares in issue excluding 20m treasury shares at 30 June 2026 (interim note 7, footnote 1) plus 2m dilutive options/awards (note 7.2). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. Buybacks (£2.1bn H1 2026, a further £1.35bn running to Feb 2027) are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and are not separately credited; cash spent after 30 June 2026 is not in the 30 June net debt, so count and bridge are on the same date.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company-defined OPERATING net debt at 30 June 2026 (interim p.22): gross borrowings 13,511 less lease liabilities 614 = 12,897 (total_debt); cash 4,056 less 1,277 set aside for regulatory and operational purposes = 2,779 free cash, plus 136 net derivative financial assets = 2,915 (cash). 12,897 - 2,915 = 9,982. Leases are excluded from debt because the full lease payment is charged inside EBIT (treatment B). Regulatory cash is excluded because it is not distributable. Clearing-member balances (~£750-850bn of matched assets/liabilities) are neither cash nor debt and are ignored.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 operating cash flow 3,622 less capex 985 (Metrics.csv). Under UK IFRS the company's OCF is AFTER net interest paid (~£187m) and after cash tax (£396m) and excludes the one-off £921m SwapClear intangible payment (kpis: SwapClearIntangiblePayment). The unlevered FY0 owner FCF on the model's lease-as-cost basis is ~2,487 (= 2,637 + 187 net interest - 176 SBC - 161 lease principal), 26.6% of total income; the component build's year-1 margin should be read against that figure.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report consolidated cash flow statement, share-based payments add-back £176m (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp). No separate equity-award tax line is disclosed; UK filers settle via the Employee Benefit Trust so the add-back is the full cost. Includes Tradeweb's own SBC (~£80m, statement of changes in equity NCI column).
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income £153m (FY2025) is NOT stripped: the group carries £10bn of operating net debt, so cash is not being double-counted via the bridge. Net treasury income on clearing collateral (£257m) is operating income inside total income and adjusted EBITDA and is left in the flows.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow £2,072m by LSEG plc (plus £80m Tradeweb). H1 2026: £2,087m LSEG + £180m Tradeweb. Repurchaser: the flat count is funded.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; the LSE quote is pence sterling (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP per share to quoted pence. No FX conversion risk and no dual listing to parity-check; the magnitude check is that a per-share value in the 60-130 GBP range must print as 6,000-13,000p against a 8,694p price. Note the business itself is ~45% USD-earning, so GBP-reported income carries translation exposure (2026 guidance struck at GBPUSD 1.32).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T16:00:15Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API, LSEG.L)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP, the currency of the flows: 10y gilt ~4.5%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.85 (subscription-heavy FMI) gives a cost of equity ~8.75%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.8% (A/A3 rated, March 2026 USD bonds) less 25% UK tax ~3.6%; market equity ~£42.6bn against ~£10bn operating net debt gives D/V ~19%. Blended ~7.8%, rounded up to 8.0% in all three scenarios. Risk is charged once, in the flows: no scenario-specific WACC and no ad-hoc premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease_cost_pct_path charges the full lease payment (principal £161m + interest ~£25m FY2025; H1 2026 lease payments £95m) inside EBIT at ~1.9% of total income, and lease liabilities (£614m) are excluded from total_debt. D&A for the cash-tax line is adjusted D&A ex right-of-use depreciation: FY2025 adjusted D&A 1,017 (adj EBITDA 4,523 - AOP 3,506) less ROU depreciation 139 (78 property + 61 other, PPE note) = 878, 9.4% of total income. The £1,221m non-underlying amortisation of Refinitiv purchased intangibles is excluded from D&A entirely: it is not an economic cost that capex has to replace.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows. Non-controlling interests (Tradeweb ~49% not owned, LCH Group ~5% after the July 2026 €70m minority purchases, Post Trade Solutions 20% held by 11 banks since 2025) took £334m of FY2025 adjusted profit and £194m in H1 2026 (+24%, Tradeweb-led), ~10% of lease-adjusted EBIT. cash_tax_rate_path is therefore a COMBINED tax-plus-NCI leakage rate: FY2026 cash tax ~12.5% of EBIT (H1 2026 taxes paid £244m) plus NCI ~10%, ramping to 24.5% tax (guided underlying ETR 24-25%; the gap between cash and P&L tax is US tax amortisation of the Refinitiv/Thomson Reuters F&R step-up, which runs out around 2033) plus 10.5% NCI (Tradeweb outgrowing the group) by year 8. No NCI deduction is made in the bridge. Cross-check: deducting the Tradeweb minority at MARKET value (~£9-11bn) instead would cut ~£8-10/share, because Tradeweb trades at roughly twice the group's multiple; that is a sum-of-parts view of Tradeweb's premium, not an owner-FCF view, and is recorded as a risk rather than modelled.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US adaptations (GBP WACC, lease treatment B, NCI as leakage, GBp quote). LSEG is an operating company: ~70% of income is recurring subscription (Data & Analytics, FTSE Russell, Risk Intelligence) and the rest is exchange, Tradeweb and LCH clearing fees. It is NOT a bank or deposit-taker: clearing-member margin and default-fund balances are matched assets and liabilities held for days, not funding for the business, and are excluded from every ratio; net treasury income on them is an operating revenue line (rate-sensitive, named as a bear axis). A residual-income or FCFE-at-CoE route would be wrong here because the flows are genuine operating free cash flow with a conventional capital structure (A-rated bonds, 2.1x leverage). Memory has no prior entry for LSEG.L; this is the first valuation. LSEG.L_Analysis.json (read after the first build) confirms the scenario axes: AI/LLM disintermediation of Data & Analytics (42% of income) as the bear axis, with two AI-driven selloffs in 2026; growth increasingly carried by volume-linked Markets; SwapClear revenue-share one-off inflating the H1 margin; 2.1x leverage with heavy buybacks; Elliott Management activism over the valuation gap to S&P Global/MSCI/ICE as a bull-side catalyst. Statutory revenue/EBITDA/EPS in core_metrics are distorted by £1.0-1.5bn/yr of Refinitiv PPA amortisation and the FY2021 continuity break (Refinitiv acquisition, Borsa Italiana disposal, £2.6bn one-off gain); all margins here are struck on the kpis' adjusted series. Working capital capture set to 0: subscription prepayments give a small deferred-revenue inflow but FY2025 showed a ~£160m net WC/non-underlying outflow and H1 is seasonally negative, so no growth tailwind is credited. Dividend of 55p interim (ex 13 Aug 2026) is already paid out of the June cash position.
inputs.guidance_anchor: FY2026 (raised at H1, 31 July 2026): organic cc growth in total income ex recoveries 7.0-7.5%; cc adjusted EBITDA margin +c.100bps on FY2025's 50.3%; capex intensity c.9.5% of income ex recoveries; equity FCF at least £2.7bn at GBPUSD 1.32; underlying ETR 24-25%. Medium term 2027-2029: mid-to-high single digit organic growth, cumulative +c.150bps underlying EBITDA margin, capex falling to c.8% by 2029, double-digit EFCF/share CAGR. Q1 2026 organic growth was 9.8% and H1 8.3%, with a timing benefit management says largely reverses in Q4.

base.growth_note: FY2026 6.5% reported GBP growth on total income: 7.0-7.5% organic ex recoveries, less ~0.5pp from flat recoveries and a GBP translation headwind at 1.32. 2027-29 at the midpoint of 'mid to high single digit' fading to 3% by year 10 as subscription growth converges on nominal GDP plus pricing.
base.margin_note: +130bps in FY2026 (guided +c.100bps cc plus the SwapClear revenue-share annualisation visible in H1's 52.7%), then +50bps/yr 2027-29 per the cumulative +150bps framework, drifting to 54% by year 7 and flat thereafter.
base.capex_da_note: Capex 9.8% of total income in FY2026 (guided c.9.5% of income ex recoveries, scaled to the CSV capex basis which runs ~7% above the company's 'cash capex'), falling to 8.4% by 2029 per the c.8% guidance; D&A ex-ROU converges down to capex so no terminal tax shield is created from D&A exceeding reinvestment.
base.tax_note: Combined cash-tax + NCI leakage, see inputs.nci_treatment. 22.5% in FY2026 = ~12.5% cash tax + ~10% NCI; ramps 1.5pp/yr as the US tax amortisation of acquired intangibles unwinds, to 35% = 24.5% + 10.5% from year 9.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the house 15/50/35 to 25/50/25. Bear up because the AI-disintermediation axis for data terminals is structural, live and unproven either way, and it hits the ~70% subscription base rather than a cyclical line; there is no solvency or covenant element to it. Bull down because it needs AI monetisation, continued Tradeweb outgrowth and above-guidance margin to coincide. Base at 50%: management has beaten or met every stated guide since 2023 and raised twice in 2025 and once in 2026.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
